subject: Workload playbook: SLO calibration & throughput heuristics
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Devlin <alex.devlin@finex.io>, ops@finex.io
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Workload playbook: SLO calibration & throughput heuristics

Hi Alex / Finex team — thanks for the time today. Quick post-call recap and the immediate next steps so we all stay aligned. TL;DR: we'll produce a short "workload playbook" with recommended SLO targets, deployment guardrails, and the telemetry template we need from your side.

Call highlights (what we captured):
- Latency targets: p50 ~120ms, p95 target <=350ms for typical requests (~512 tokens). Streaming sessions need to see first-byte within 120–150ms and subsequent chunks at ~100–200ms cadence.
- Throughput profile: steady-state ~120 QPS (typical weekday traffic), peak planned bursts up to ~800 QPS (10-minute windows during batch runs).
- Token distribution: average ~320 tokens/request today; we estimated steady-state token rate at ~38,400 tokens/sec (120 QPS * 320 tokens) and peak token rate ~256,000 tokens/sec (800 QPS * 320 tokens). We noted you have a long-tail of heavier requests — please confirm 95th/99th token sizes from your logs.
- Streaming & concurrency: 20% of traffic is streaming-enabled; concurrency for active streaming sessions observed at ~60 concurrent streams during peak in our call.
- Failure/fallback behavior: you asked about automatic fallbacks to smaller model variants for cost/availability — we can configure policy-based fallbacks and will document typical tradeoffs.

Attachments included from today's upload: finex-workload-snapshot-10122026.csv (sample traces), sla-profiles-draft.pdf (initial SLO wording).

Next steps (owners & timelines):
1) Redwood: produce a 1–2 page Playbook summarizing SLOs, recommended Dedicated pool sizing, autoscale knobs, and fallback policies — delivery by Tue 2026-10-14. (Owner: lauren_bishop)
2) Finex: share token-size histogram (95/99 percentiles), percent streaming sessions by endpoint, and any long-tail endpoint labels by Fri 2026-10-16. (Owner: ops@finex.io)
3) Technical deep dive: schedule a 60-minute follow-up to walk the playbook and capacity estimates (Finex requested week of Oct 19). (Owner: all)

Open questions we want answers to before the deep dive:
- Confirm percent of requests that can be truncated vs must be fully completed (impacts caching & batching).
- Confirm acceptable per-request max latency for the long 2k+ token interactions (5% of traffic per your note).

If that aligns with your notes, we'll push the playbook and a first-pass capacity workbook to the Drive link and HubSpot deal record.

Thanks again — Lauren

--

Subject: Re: Workload playbook: SLO calibration & throughput heuristics

Lauren — thanks for the crisp recap, that matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Token distribution: the 320 tokens/request average is right for our web UI flows, but we have a smaller set of "long form" jobs (about 5% of requests) that can be 1.5k–2.5k tokens. Those are non-interactive batch jobs and can be queued differently if needed.

- Streaming: we require streaming for the customer-facing chat widget (low latency) and also allow for non-streamed batch outputs. When streaming, the client expects incremental outputs roughly every 100–200ms after the initial first-byte.

- Fallbacks: yes — automatic fallback to a smaller quantized variant is preferred to dropping requests. Can you confirm whether prefix caching will still be effective when we fallback? Also what is the expected quality degradation we should plan for (e.g., token-level differences or hallucination risk)?

- Timeline: procurement is aggressive — headed for a PO by Nov 15 if we can lock SLOs and pricing.

Appreciate the playbook. Can we lock a 1-hour technical deep dive the week of Oct 19 (we prefer Oct 20 morning ET)?

Thanks,
Alex

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Workload playbook: SLO calibration & throughput heuristics

Lauren / Marissa — quick technical notes to include in the playbook and the workbook I'm drafting. Please review before we send the playbook to Finex.

1) Capacity assumptions (ballpark, conservative):
   - Measured GPU token throughput (mixed 8-bit kernels on Ampere-like hardware): ~60k tokens/sec per GPU when serving primarily short-medium responses and with KV-cache hits.
   - For Finex steady-state: 38.4k tokens/sec => recommend 1x GPU to cover baseline (60k throughput) but plan headroom.
   - Peak (256k tokens/sec) => ~4.3 GPUs raw; with batching/streaming inefficiencies and redundancy we should recommend 6 GPUs reserved with autoscale to 8 for safety.

2) Streaming behavior: streaming reduces batching efficiency; expect 20–30% throughput loss for flows where interleaved streaming is dominant. For the 20% streaming fraction noted, plan mixing strategy in the runtime (dedicated streaming lanes vs batch lanes).

3) Fallbacks & caching: prefix/KV caching remains effective if the model family is the same and tokenizer alignment is preserved. If fallback is to a model with different tokenizer/architecture, cache effectiveness drops significantly. Document policy: allow fallback only to verified compatible variants (we'll propose a compatible quantized variant).

4) Actionables for Finex to expedite sizing:
   - Provide token-size histogram (0/25/50/75/95/99) by Oct 16.
   - Mark endpoints that require strict streaming SLOs vs endpoints that are best-effort.

I'll attach the capacity worksheet I'm preparing. This contains a per-endpoint worksheet and a suggested Dedicated pool config.

Jonas

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Workload playbook: SLO calibration & throughput heuristics

Alex — answering your specific questions and laying out the recommended next steps. Quoting your note inline where helpful.

> "Can you confirm whether prefix caching will still be effective when we fallback?"
Short answer: yes if the fallback variant uses the same tokenizer and model family. Jonas pulled quick numbers: switching to a compatible quantized variant preserves most cache hits; switching architecture/tokenizer will invalidate cached KV pairs. We'll enumerate compatible fallback candidates in the Playbook.

> "What is the expected quality degradation?"
We'll include qualitative guidance in the Playbook: expect some token-level variance and slightly different phrasing from quantized variants, but for many of your transactional endpoints quality delta should be minimal. We'll attach examples in a short A/B prompt test.

Recommended initial configuration (summary):
- Deployment: Redwood Dedicated pool (reserved) sized to 6 GPUs baseline, autoscale +2 for burst headroom (8 total).
- Autoscale policy: step scale at 60% and 85% token-rate thresholds; prefer scheduled scale-up during known batch windows.
- Routing: streaming-dedicated lane for chat widget; batch lane for long jobs so they don't harm streaming latency.
- SLOs: p50 120ms, p95 <=350ms for interactive; first-byte streaming target <=150ms.

Links: playbook (draft) and capacity workbook will be at: https://drive.google.com/finex/workload-playbook and I'll attach to HubSpot (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-9982).

Proposed timeline: playbook & workbook to you by EOD 2026-10-14; technical deep dive Wed Oct 20 11:00–12:00 ET if that works for your team.

Let us know if you'd like us to include an estimated cost delta for the different autoscale strategies in the workbook.

Thanks — Lauren
